title: Zone-split traffic steering and throughput safeguards for dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a 'zone-split' steering layer and per-tenant throughput safeguards for multi-zone Dedicated pools. Goal: allow customers to request dedicated capacity with regional placement preferences (soft and hard constraints), guarantee per-tenant throughput SLOs across zones, and provide predictable failover semantics while enforcing data residency via egress controls. This ticket covers the routing policy proto, autoscale interaction rules, admission/circuit-breaker heuristics, and the observable signals required to operate the feature in production.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy supports soft-preference and hard-residency modes with explicit zone weights
Per-tenant throughput lanes enforced at the dispatcher with clear throttles and token accounting
Autoscaler uses traffic-steering signals to pre-warm capacity in preferred zones within configured lead-time
Failover converts soft-preference -> cross-zone spill with bounded additional latency and documented egress checks
End-to-end e2e test validates a tenant with residency constraint never routes requests to disallowed zones
Console shows per-tenant zone distribution, throughput lane usage, and failover events in the route dashboard
implementation_notes: Add a new RoutingPolicy object (protobuf) with fields: mode={soft, hard}, zone_weights map, max_cross_zone_qps, preferred_zone_sequence
Introduce per-tenant ThroughputLane token-bucket at the dispatcher; lane is evaluated before batching to preserve SLO
Autoscaler hook: expose a "zone_prewarm_score" metric derived from moving-average QPS + lane utilization to allow predictive pre-warming
Admission controller enforces residence: attach egress-region metadata to runtime nodes; dispatcher checks allowed_regions for tenant before issuing to node
Circuit-breaker policy: when preferred-zone latency percentile > threshold or node drain ongoing, spill fraction increases gradually (10% steps) until failover cap
Backward compatibility: default routing policy for existing tenants is 'soft' with equal zone_weights to avoid behavior change
Implement feature flags: runtime.routing.zone_split_v1 and console.ui.zone_distribution_v1 for staged rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable routing.zone_split_v1 for internal test tenant in us-east/asia-multi-zone cluster - validate metrics and egress enforcement
Stage 2 (pilot): open to 5 beta customers with mixed residency constraints; monitor throughput lane saturation and prewarm success
Stage 3 (wider): enable for all Dedicated customers with opt-in via console; default keep legacy behavior until 2-week stable window
Fallback procedure: manual toggle to disable zone_split_v1 + rollback of routing table; automated re-route to prior primary zone for hard-residency tenants
Post-rollout: 30-day observation window with weekly ops review and rollback criteria (sustained >2% error increase or >10% latency regressions for high-priority tenants)
test_plan: Unit tests: routing policy serialization, token-bucket accounting, admission checks for residency
Integration tests: simulated multi-zone cluster with configurable latencies; validate progressive spill and prewarm triggers
E2E: tenant configured hard-residency -> synthetic load from disallowed region should be rejected and logged; soft-preference -> gradual spill observed
Chaos test: forced draining of preferred-zone nodes; ensure circuit-breaker increments spill fraction and autoscaler pre-warms target zone within configured SLA
Security test: verify egress metadata cannot be spoofed by injecting nodes and that KMS access logs capture residency policy changes
monitoring_metrics: residency.violations.count (should remain zero for hard-residency tenants)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: unintended egress to disallowed zones due to misconfiguration. Mitigation: strict admission checks, automated audits, and a daily residency compliance job
Risk: oscillation between zones causing higher overall latency. Mitigation: dampened spill increments, hysteresis windows, and min-stability timers before reversing decisions
Risk: throughput lane starvation for high-priority tenants during autoscaler cold starts. Mitigation: predictive pre-warming using zone_prewarm_score and a small reserved burst pool per-tenant
Risk: increased cost from pre-warming. Mitigation: configurable prewarm_lead_time and cost caps per customer; show cost implications in the console before enabling
Risk: complex debugging surface for SRE. Mitigation: add end-to-end tracing id propagation for routing decisions and provide a "routing replay" tool in internal ops UI
comments: 2025-02-13 | Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and architecture sketch attached to Confluence. Captured two routing modes (soft/hard) and proposed per-tenant lanes. Requesting engineering triage.

2025-02-20 | Luca Moretti: Reviewed with infra & autoscaler teams. Agreed to adopt token-bucket lanes and add prewarm hook. Need clarification on retention of per-tenant counters - will prefer 7 days to keep cardinality manageable.
2025-02-27 | Priya Nair (Product): Customer-facing constraints clarified: beta customers expect explicit cost estimates for pre-warm. Add console projection card before opt-in.

2025-03-02 | SRE (review): Raised concern about tracing — recommended a unique routing-decision-id header and a replay log stored for 14 days. Also suggested canary with synthetic failover every 6 hours.

2025-03-04 | Luca Moretti: Implementation plan approved. Creating sub-tasks for dispatcher, autoscaler, admission-controller, console UI and playbook. Security review request submitted (ticket SEC-1123).
